questions.q: How are container images tagged in this pipeline, and why?
options: Always tagged `latest`, for simplicity
Tagged with `${{ github.sha }}`, so every image in ACR is traceable to the exact commit that produced it
Tagged with a random UUID
Not tagged at all
questions.explain: SHA-tagging means any image can be traced back to the commit that built it, which matters for rollbacks.

questions.q: How does the deploy job authenticate to Azure?
options: With a long-lived client secret stored in GitHub Secrets
With an OIDC federated credential — GitHub issues a short-lived token that Azure AD exchanges for a short-lived access token
By prompting a human to type in a password during the workflow run
It doesn't need to authenticate; AKS is public
questions.explain: azure/login@v2 here uses OIDC token exchange, so there is no stored client secret to steal or rotate.

questions.q: What does `helm upgrade --install` do on the very first deploy versus every deploy after?
options: It fails on the first deploy and only works afterward
It creates the release on the first run and upgrades it in place on every subsequent run — the same command either way
It requires a different command for the first deploy
It deletes the cluster and recreates it every time
questions.explain: `helm upgrade --install` is idempotent: the same command works whether this is deploy #1 or deploy #400.

questions.q: Does this pipeline re-derive or question the autoscaling numbers in `values-prod.yaml` before deploying?
options: Yes, it recalculates them from live traffic before every deploy
No — it applies whatever is currently in that file faithfully, every single time, without questioning it
It asks Casey to approve the numbers manually each time
It ignores `values-prod.yaml` entirely and uses hardcoded defaults
questions.explain: The pipeline's job is to apply values-prod.yaml exactly as written on every deploy — including whatever autoscaling numbers it already contains.

questions.q: What does the smoke test step do after `helm upgrade --install` runs?
options: Nothing; there is no smoke test in this pipeline
It waits for the rollout to finish and checks a health endpoint before the deploy counts as successful
It deletes the deployment if a test fails
It only runs once per week, not on every deploy
questions.explain: `kubectl rollout status` plus a health-endpoint curl gate the deploy so a broken rollout doesn't silently pass as a success.
